Reference / http/cookie

http/cookie#

Cookies (RFC 6265bis): Set-Cookie on the way out, Cookie on the way in.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

Response(status: Status.ok, headers: Headers(
    SetCookie(name: "sid", value: token),
    SetCookie(name: "theme", value: "dark", max_age: Duration(days: 30)),
));
Headers(ExpiredCookie("sid"));                     // removes it

let cookies = RequestCookies(request);
cookies.text("sid");                               // MissingCookie when absent
cookies.maybe("theme").text() else "light";

Description#

Cookies (RFC 6265bis): Set-Cookie on the way out, Cookie on the way in.

SetCookie(name, value) is safe by default: Path=/, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Build a Cookie with CookieAttributes to say otherwise. A cookie without an expiry is a session cookie. Values are redacted in diagnostics.

object CookieAttributes#

object CookieAttributes

Names retain case; the prefix checks follow the case-insensitive consumer policy of RFC 6265bis draft-22. cross_site renders the wire token None because none is the language's null literal. A constructor snapshots role flags before retaining them, and explicit string() rendering is the only payload diagnostic.

object SetCookie#

object SetCookie does HeaderField

A Set-Cookie field of a response, with safe defaults: Path=/, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, and Max-Age when it is given (#207):

Headers(SetCookie(name: "sid", value: token),
    SetCookie(name: "theme", value: "dark", max_age: Duration(days: 30)))

SetCookie(cookie) sends a Cookie with exactly its own attributes.

object RequestCookies#

object RequestCookies

The cookies a client sent in its Cookie fields, read by name on the server (#206): name=value pairs separated by semicolons (RFC 6265 5.4). A value in double quotes loses them; a pair without "=" is skipped; with one name twice, text() takes the first, as browsers send the more specific cookie first.

let cookies = RequestCookies(request);
let session = cookies.text("sid");
let theme = cookies.maybe("theme").text() else "light";
